headline: Visayas Grid Under Red and Yellow Alerts as Available Supply Falls Below Peak Demand
seoTitle: Visayas Grid Red, Yellow Alerts Aug. 28 | FMB News
seoDescription: NGCP placed the Visayas grid under Red and Yellow Alerts on August 28 as available capacity stood at 2,307 MW against projected peak demand of 2,402 MW.
deck: NGCP scheduled a Red Alert from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m., with Yellow Alerts before and after the evening peak, amid plant outages and limited imports from Mindanao.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Visayas grid remained under Red and Yellow Alerts on Friday because available electricity supply was insufficient for projected demand and contingency requirements, according to the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines.
NGCP estimated available capacity at 2,307 megawatts against projected peak demand of about 2,402 MW.

sections.heading: Alert schedule
paragraphs: The Red Alert was scheduled from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Yellow Alerts were scheduled from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. and from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m.

A Red Alert means supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the grid's regulating requirement. A Yellow Alert means the operating margin is insufficient to meet the grid's contingency requirement.

sections.heading: Why supply is tight
paragraphs: NGCP said several coal-fired power plants, including units of Therma Visayas Inc. and KEPCO SPC Power Corp., were on forced outage. Electricity imports from Mindanao were also limited.
Ten power plants were unavailable during August and 16 other plants were operating at derated capacities, bringing unavailable or reduced capacity to about 979.6 MW.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Visayas grid has experienced repeated Yellow and Red Alerts in recent months as demand, forced outages, maintenance and reduced plant output have tightened operating reserves.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated grid alerts increase the risk of service interruptions and can raise system costs when utilities must rely on more expensive replacement supply during tight periods.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Consumers and businesses should monitor NGCP and distribution-utility advisories for changes in alert schedules, possible interruptions and restoration of unavailable generating units.
